knowledge:
- key_parameters: normal.sigma=Scaling parameter where decreasing normal.sigma is equivalent to increasing sigma and vice versa; must be tuned until the eigenvalue curve shows a knee shape (e.g., 250) ;; separation.factor=Controls post-processing cluster merging where larger values (e.g., 0.5) keep populations separated and smaller values (e.g., 0.1) combine them ;; m=Number of representative communities to build, typically set to 3000 to keep runtimes under 1 minute ;; community.weakness.threshold=Threshold for community weakness, typically set to 1 ;; precision=Precision parameter for conductance calculation, typically set to 6 ;; maximum.number.of.clusters=Maximum number of spectral clusters to search for, typically set to 30 ;; eigenvalues.num=Number of top eigenvalues to consider for fitting regression lines (e.g., 50) ;; one.line=Logical flag; if TRUE, fits only one regression line to estimate spectral clusters, which can lead to overestimation but may perform better after post-processing merging
- alternatives: Standard spectral clustering (computationally prohibitive for large datasets due to memory and time limitations)
- when_to_use: When clustering large flow cytometry datasets where clusters have arbitrary shapes, noise, or outliers, and standard spectral clustering is too slow or memory-intensive
- pitfalls: Setting normal.sigma too low (e.g., 10) results in an eigenvalue curve without a knee shape; setting it too high (e.g., 1000) results in too many eigenvalues close to 1. Setting separation.factor too low (e.g., 0.1) can combine distinct populations by mistake.

workflows.name: quick_samspectral_clustering
workflows.intent: Run the complete SamSPECTRAL clustering pipeline using the high-level wrapper function on a flow cytometry data matrix.
input: flow_data.csv (A matrix or data frame of coordinates, e.g., expression matrix from a flowFrame)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the package and data ;; 2. Run the SamSPECTRAL wrapper function with specified dimensions, normal.sigma, and separation.factor ;; 3. Calculate cluster frequencies and plot results
workflows.code:
library(SamSPECTRAL)
set.seed(4)
data(small_data)
full <- small

L <- SamSPECTRAL(full,dimension=c(1,2,3),normal.sigma = 200,
                 separation.factor = 0.39)   
plot(full, pch='.', col= L)

plot(full, pch='.', col= L)
frequency <- c()	
minimum.frequency <- 0.01	
freq.large <- c()	
labels <- as.character(unique(L))
for(label in labels){
  if(!is.na(label)){
    frequency[label] <- length(which(L==label))/length(L)
    if(frequency[label] > minimum.frequency)
      freq.large[label] <- frequency[label]
  }
}	
print(frequency)	

legend(x="topleft",as.character(round(freq.large,3)),
       col=names(freq.large),pch=19)

workflows.name: step_by_step_parameter_tuning
workflows.intent: Manually tune parameters (sigma and separation factor) and run the step-by-step SamSPECTRAL pipeline for precise clustering control.
input: flow_data.csv (A matrix or data frame of coordinates, e.g., expression matrix from a flowFrame)
workflows.stages: 1. Scale coordinates to the range [0,1] ;; 2. Build communities using Building_Communities ;; 3. Calculate conductance using Conductance_Calculation with a trial normal.sigma ;; 4. Perform spectral clustering using Civilized_Spectral_Clustering and plot eigenvalues to find the knee point ;; 5. Adjust normal.sigma and repeat until the eigenvalue curve has a knee shape ;; 6. Extract labels and post-process using Connecting with an adjusted separation.factor
workflows.code:
data(small_data)
full <- small

m <- 3000; 
community.weakness.threshold <-1; precision <- 6; 
maximum.number.of.clusters <- 30    

for (i.column in 1:dim(full)[2]){#For all columns
  ith.col <- full[,i.column]
  full[,i.column] <- (ith.col-min(ith.col)) /(max(ith.col) - min(ith.col) )  
}#End for (i.column.
space.length <- 1

society <- 
    Building_Communities(full,m, space.length, community.weakness.threshold)
plot(full[society$representatives, ], pch=20)

normal.sigma <- 10
conductance <- Conductance_Calculation(full, normal.sigma, space.length, 
                                       society, precision)

normal.sigma <- 1000
conductance <- Conductance_Calculation(full, normal.sigma, space.length, society, precision)

normal.sigma <- 250
conductance <- Conductance_Calculation(full, normal.sigma, space.length, 
                                       society, precision)
clust_result.250 <- 
    Civilized_Spectral_Clustering(full, maximum.number.of.clusters, 
                                  society, conductance,stabilizer=1)    
eigen.values.250 <- clust_result.250@eigen.space$values
plot(eigen.values.250[1:50])

clust_result.250 <- 
    Civilized_Spectral_Clustering(full, maximum.number.of.clusters, 
                                  society, conductance,stabilizer=1,
                                  eigenvalues.num=50)    

clust_result.250 <- 
    Civilized_Spectral_Clustering(full, maximum.number.of.clusters, 
                                  society, conductance,stabilizer=1,
                                  eigenvalues.num=50, one.line=TRUE)

labels.for_num.of.clusters <- clust_result.250@labels.for_num.of.clusters
number.of.clusters <- clust_result.250@number.of.clusters
L33 <- labels.for_num.of.clusters[[number.of.clusters]]
separation.factor <- 0.1
component.of <- 
    Connecting(full, society, conductance, number.of.clusters, 
               labels.for_num.of.clusters, separation.factor)$label
plot(full, pch='.', col= component.of)

separation.factor <- 0.5
component.of <- 
    Connecting(full, society, conductance, number.of.clusters, 
               labels.for_num.of.clusters, separation.factor)$label
plot(full, pch='.', col= component.of)
